overall_summary: Markets lean bearish for Bitcoin as renewed US-Iran strikes and oil spikes revive inflation fears, pushing yields higher and reinforcing risk-off pressure. Fed minutes showing some openness to rate hikes compound the headwinds, while ETF outflows add direct selling pressure. Institutional positives like SWIFT's blockchain pilot and SEC rule progress provide only limited offset.
key_points: Bitcoin ETFs flip to net outflows
Oil spikes on US-Iran conflict escalate inflation fears
Higher yields and Fed hike talk pressure risk assets
SWIFT blockchain pilot and Brazil crypto options positive
SEC advances July crypto rules agenda

items.title: SWIFT Launches Blockchain Ledger Pilot with 17 Banks
items.summary: SWIFT has activated its blockchain-based shared ledger for live pilots with 17 major banks including Citi, HSBC, UBS, Wells Fargo, and others across six continents. The system enables 24/7 cross-border payments using tokenized bank deposits while keeping final settlement on traditional rails. Traders should care because this is traditional finance deeply integrating blockchain infrastructure at scale, which strengthens the case for tokenized assets and regulated digital money over the long run.
items.impact: Boosts institutional blockchain and tokenization adoption narrative

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Flip to $84 Million Outflow After Inflow Streak
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net outflow of about 84 to 85 million dollars on Wednesday, July 8, ending a three-day inflow run that had brought in roughly 509 million. BlackRock IBIT and Grayscale led the redemptions while Ether ETFs extended their inflow streak with about 70 million, mostly into Fidelity FETH. This matters for traders because ETF flows remain a key institutional demand signal and the flip back to outflows removes near-term buying pressure on Bitcoin.
items.impact: Weakens short-term institutional demand for Bitcoin

items.title: Crypto Holds Firm Despite US-Iran Escalation and Trump Remarks
items.summary: Bitcoin and major cryptos came under initial pressure after US airstrikes on Iran and President Trump declaring the ceasefire over, sending oil higher and risk assets lower, with BTC dipping toward 61 to 62 thousand. Markets later recovered, with Bitcoin reclaiming levels near 63 thousand and showing overall resilience, up about 9 percent since end of June. Traders should watch this because it tests Bitcoin's risk-off correlation; the limited damage so far suggests some decoupling or strong underlying demand.
items.impact: Geopolitical risk premium stays elevated but no confirmed breakdown

items.title: Brazil B3 Launches Options on Bitcoin Ether Solana Futures
items.summary: Latin America's largest stock exchange B3 has introduced options on its Bitcoin, Ether, and Solana futures contracts, available since July 6. The options settle into the futures rather than spot crypto, avoiding custody issues, and give local traders regulated tools for hedging and volatility trading. This expands institutional and retail access to crypto derivatives in a major emerging market and could increase overall liquidity and product sophistication for BTC and majors.
items.impact: Expands regulated crypto derivatives access in Latin America

items.title: SEC Advances Crypto Rules and Safe Harbor Agenda for July
items.summary: The SEC updated its 2026 regulatory agenda to include key crypto rulemaking items covering asset offerings, broker-dealer treatment, trading venues, and temporary safe harbors or exemptions for startups and DeFi-related activities. Regulation Crypto or similar proposals are teed up for public comment as soon as this month under Chair Atkins. Clearer rules reduce uncertainty for institutions and builders, which has historically been a positive catalyst for crypto markets when delivered constructively.
items.impact: Potential regulatory clarity catalyst for US crypto activity

items.title: Temasek Keeps Crypto Off Table While Prioritizing AI
items.summary: Singapore's sovereign wealth fund Temasek, managing hundreds of billions, reiterated that direct crypto investments remain off the table, citing past FTX losses and ongoing regulatory uncertainty, while ramping up AI allocations toward 15 percent of the portfolio. This comes as other institutional stories mix positive and cautious signals. Traders should note it as a reminder that not all large allocators are rushing back into crypto, potentially capping some institutional bid strength.
items.impact: Signals continued caution from major sovereign capital

items.title: FOMC Minutes Show Fed Split, Some Eye Rate Hikes
items.summary: The Federal Reserve released minutes from its June meeting showing policymakers divided on the path of interest rates. Some officials saw a case for hiking rates this year amid elevated inflation from energy shocks and AI demand, while others envisioned possible cuts if inflation eases. The committee held rates steady at 3.5 to 3.75 percent and dropped prior easing language. Crypto traders should watch closely because a higher-for-longer or hawkish pivot would tighten financial conditions and pressure risk assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Supports higher yields and stronger dollar, headwinds for crypto

items.title: Oil Jumps on US-Iran Conflict, Reigniting Inflation Fears
items.summary: Oil prices surged after President Trump declared the interim Iran ceasefire over following US strikes and threats around the Strait of Hormuz. Brent climbed toward 78-80 dollars a barrel, with shipping nearly grinding to a halt. This renews supply-driven inflation risks just as the Fed debates its next move. Traders care because sticky energy prices could force the Fed to stay hawkish or hike, lifting yields and weighing on risk appetite across markets including crypto.
items.impact: Higher inflation premium pressures bonds and risk assets

items.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Near Multi-Week High at 4.57%
items.summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield hovered around 4.57 to 4.58 percent, near its highest since late May, as oil spikes and hawkish Fed minutes fueled inflation and rate-hike bets. Markets now price a higher chance of at least one hike later in 2026. Bond moves like this matter for crypto because rising yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets and often correlate with tighter liquidity and dollar strength.
items.impact: Tighter financial conditions, headwind for Bitcoin and equities

items.title: China June CPI Eases to 1.0% as PPI Hits Multi-Year High
items.summary: China's consumer inflation slowed to 1.0 percent year-over-year in June, below the 1.1 percent consensus and down from 1.2 percent in May, with food prices still soft. Producer prices, however, jumped to a roughly four-year high around 4 percent amid energy costs. Soft CPI eases pressure for aggressive Chinese stimulus while high PPI squeezes manufacturers. For global markets this is mixed but overall points to uneven global inflation that could keep major central banks cautious.
items.impact: Limited immediate boost to risk assets; mixed China demand signal

items.title: Dollar Index Steady Near 101 Resistance on Yields
items.summary: The US Dollar Index held firm around 100.8 to 101, testing resistance as Treasury yields rose and geopolitical risks supported safe-haven flows. It has absorbed higher rates without a clean breakout yet. A stronger dollar typically pressures gold, emerging markets, and crypto by tightening global dollar liquidity. Traders should monitor whether it breaks higher on today's data or speeches.
items.impact: Dollar strength often coincides with crypto weakness

items.title: Jobless Claims and Home Sales Due; Fed Speakers Today
items.summary: Markets await weekly initial jobless claims for the week ending July 4, consensus around 218,000 versus prior 215,000, plus June existing home sales expected near 4.2 million. New York Fed's John Williams and Dallas Fed's Lorie Logan also speak. Soft claims would signal labor resilience supporting a higher-for-longer Fed, while weak housing could hint at rate sensitivity. These are classic market movers that can swing yields, the dollar, and risk assets intraday.
items.impact: Data-dependent volatility for rates and crypto pricing

items.title: US-Iran Strikes Resume as Trump Declares Ceasefire Over
items.summary: The United States launched a new wave of airstrikes on roughly ninety Iranian military targets for a second straight day, hitting ports and coastal sites near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran fired back with drones and missiles at US bases in Bahrain and Kuwait. President Trump, speaking from the NATO summit, said the interim ceasefire deal is over after Iranian attacks on shipping, warning strikes could get much worse. Traders should care because this reopens major energy chokepoint risk and injects fresh geopolitical volatility into global markets.
items.impact: Heightened war premium and risk-off pressure on equities and crypto

items.title: Oil Prices Jump Sharply on Renewed Hormuz Threats
items.summary: Brent crude rose more than five percent and hit multi-week highs after Trump said the Iran ceasefire was finished and fresh US strikes hit Iranian facilities. Markets fear renewed disruption to the Strait of Hormuz, which handles a huge share of global oil. The Treasury also revoked a temporary waiver allowing Iranian oil sales. Higher energy costs feed inflation fears and tighten financial conditions, which historically weighs on risk assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Elevated oil and inflation risk dampens appetite for crypto and stocks

items.title: Trump Grants Ukraine License to Produce Patriot Missiles
items.summary: At the NATO summit in Ankara, President Trump told Ukrainian President Zelenskyy that the US will license Ukraine to manufacture Patriot air-defense interceptors. Production could start in a few months once supply chains are sorted. This is a major defensive boost for Kyiv against Russian ballistic missiles. For markets it signals continued Western commitment that could prolong the conflict and keep European defense spending elevated.
items.impact: Supports defense equities but keeps Ukraine war uncertainty alive

items.title: Trump Orders Halt to All US Trade with Spain
items.summary: During the NATO summit Trump called Spain a terrible partner for low defense spending and weak support on Iran, then ordered Treasury Secretary Bessent to cut off all trade including visits. He later claimed overall summit unity but the threat rattled allies. Spain is a key EU economy, so any move risks a broader US-EU trade clash. Traders should watch because fresh tariff or trade-war headlines can quickly hit risk assets and the euro.
items.impact: Trade-war fears add downside pressure to global risk sentiment

items.title: China Tests Submarine Ballistic Missile into Pacific
items.summary: China fired a nuclear-capable submarine-launched ballistic missile from the South China Sea into international waters in the Pacific on July sixth. The US State Department criticized the short notice and limited details. Japan, Australia, New Zealand and Taiwan all expressed concern, and Taiwan is stepping up coordination with partners. This keeps Indo-Pacific tensions elevated and raises the risk premium on Asian markets and supply chains that crypto traders monitor.
items.impact: Asia geopolitical risk premium weighs on global risk assets

items.title: NATO Summit Ends with Trump Praising Turkey, Criticizing Allies
items.summary: The two-day NATO summit in Ankara wrapped with Trump claiming lots of unity after earlier lashing out over Iran basing and defense spending. He warmly praised Turkish President Erdogan while renewing claims on Greenland and criticizing several European partners. Arms deals worth tens of billions were unveiled. The mixed messaging keeps alliance cohesion questions open, which can affect European risk assets and the broader geopolitical backdrop for markets.
items.impact: Uncertain alliance dynamics leave markets watching for follow-through
